subject: [PATCH v2 3/5] btrfs: pre-allocate delayed dir index before btree modification

reviews.author: Qu Wenruo
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that when a pre-allocated delayed dir index is passed to btrfs_insert_dir_item(), and an ENOMEM failure occurs before insert_with_overflow() is called, the pre-alloc memory is leaked because it is not properly released.

Reviewer Qu Wenruo noted that the preallocated memory in btrfs_prealloc_delayed_dir_index() is not utilizing the name->name field, and suggested merging the subsequent memcpy() into this function to avoid unnecessary copying.
reviews.raw_body:
This is exposed by sashiko.

If we have @prealloc passed in, and before we even hit 
insert_with_overflow(), the previous btrfs_alloc_path() failed, we 
return -ENOMEM directly, leaking the @prealloc.

---

Sashiko also pointed out that, the preallocation itself doesn't really 
utilize name->name.

Thus it may be a good idea to merge the later memcpy() into the 
preallocation function.

Thanks,
Qu

reviews.author: Jeff Layton (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that additional issues were found by Qu Wenruo and sashiko, agreed to address them in a new version (v3) of the patch series.
reviews.raw_body:
Good catch. It looks like sashiko also flagged some other similar
issues nearby too that we might as well fix while we're in here. I'll
plan to spin up a v3 and resend the series. Thanks very much for the
review so far!

-- 
Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>

2026-08-05.patch_summary: This patch improves the Btrfs file system by pre-allocating delayed directory indices before modifying the btree. This change prevents ENOMEM failures from leaving the btree in an inconsistent state, which could only be resolved by aborting the transaction. The patch introduces a new parameter to the btrfs_insert_dir_item function for caller-provided pre-allocation and removes a wrapper function that was no longer needed.
